rationale: W0 for n-heptane, one shot, literature-informed. No heptane outcome of PSI-69 was opened before this file was written: the heptane cohort and its session-grouped split were frozen from metadata first (commit c65b639). A droplet is in a hot flame, a cool flame or no flame. Hot-flame rate: hinge network on the published medians by oxygen, diluent and size. Droplets above a critical diameter (2.8 mm in air, rising steeply with oxygen) lose the hot flame to radiation after about half a diffusion-clock unit and then, with a probability that falls with helium and with oxygen below air, burn in a cool flame at about 0.85 of the hot rate down to an extinction diameter that follows [O2]^-3/4 and falls with pressure. Smaller droplets burn to a small size. Every number is a hypothesis written before the model was run on heptane; see edits.wsp.
